fields.features_heading: What a Live History Form Does Differently
fields.features_subheading: Six ways the history works once it is a live form, not a printed PDF.
fields.feature_1:
Conditions asked as yes or no

Asks about each condition as a yes or no and opens the follow-up only on a yes: the year it was diagnosed and whether it is still treated. A no moves on to the next condition.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

Shows the history one question at a time, in type large enough to read without zooming. A yes or no takes one tap, and the medication table adds a row per prescription.
fields.feature_3:
Paper histories read into fields

Reads a scanned paper history into the same fields the online form fills. Older charts sit beside new answers, and a value read with low confidence goes to staff to check first.
fields.feature_4:
A summary page for the clinician

Builds the page a clinician opens before the visit: current conditions, medications, and allergies at the top, family history below, and the full set of answers one click away.
fields.feature_5:
Answers that reach a named person

Sends a Slack or email alert to the staff member who owns an answer, such as a latex allergy to whoever preps the exam room, with reminders until someone marks it seen.
fields.feature_6:
Histories in a database you own

Keeps every history in a database you own, with no cap on the number of responses. The form connects to any tool with an API, such as the scheduling software your front desk uses.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Reads the History, and When
fields.tab_content_1:
Patients confirm or edit each section

Birchline Internal Medicine sends returning patients last year's history 7 days before the annual physical. Owen Pratt confirms four sections and edits two: a new prescription, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and a knee operation in March. Dr. Ruth Calloway opens his chart to those 2 changes first.
fields.tab_content_2:
A parent or sibling's diagnosis heads the summary

New patients at Harbor Point Family Practice add a row per relative, with the condition and the age at diagnosis. Mara Quinlan enters four relatives. Her mother's type 2 diabetes at 52 and her brother's high blood pressure at 38 open the summary Dr. Theo Aldana reads.
fields.tab_content_3:
A blood thinner or an anesthesia problem alerts the nurse

Westgate Surgery Center asks patients to finish the history 5 days before the procedure. Hana Okafor, the pre-op nurse, hears about a blood thinner on the medication list or a past problem with anesthesia. Walter Brandt lists warfarin before his hernia repair. She gets an email and calls him that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every camper who carries an auto-injector lands on one list

Parents fill in the Lakeview Day Camp health screening for each camper before day one. A yes to an epinephrine auto-injector or a medicine during camp hours puts the camper on the list for Joel Ferreira, the camp nurse. Ava Kowalski's father marks her peanut allergy and auto-injector, and the list reaches 9 campers.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Medical History Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a medical history form patients can finish on a phone and update each year, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Gather the history pages you use now
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the sections in a fixed order
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set up family history by relative
fields.howto_step_1_des: Lay out every history page patients fill in today, front and back. Next to each question, write who reads the answer and when: the doctor in the exam room, the nurse at check-in, or the surgeon before a procedure. A question with no reader comes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start with the patient's details, then current conditions, past surgeries and hospital stays, medications, allergies, family history, and tobacco and alcohol use. Keep that order every year. A returning patient and the doctor then know where to find each answer.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask your doctors which conditions they want named on the form, such as asthma or diabetes, and list those as checkboxes. End the list with one open box for anything it misses, and ask for the year that condition began.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each relative a row: mother, father, each sibling, and each grandparent. CDC's family health history guidance names major medical conditions, causes of death, and age at disease diagnosis as the details to include. Give each of the three its own column.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your sections, condition list, and alert rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the database its answers are saved to, and the summary page the clinician opens. To change a question later, describe the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give each urgent answer one owner
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the answers that cannot wait for the visit, and assign each to one named person instead of a shared inbox. Choose email or Slack for each, and name a second person to hear about it when the first is out.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as a new and a returning patient
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone twice: once as a new patient, once as a returning patient with last year's answers loaded. Change one medication on the second pass, then check that the summary marks it as a change and every alert arrives.

faq_plan.q: What does the medical history form include?
faq_plan.ref: what does the medical history form include
faq_plan.a: A medical history form includes the conditions a patient has now or has had, past operations and hospital stays, every medicine with its dose, and each allergy with the reaction it causes. A family section records illness in parents, siblings, and grandparents. The form closes with the patient's signature and the date.

faq_plan.q: How to create a medical history form?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a medical history form?

prov.original: How to create a medical history form?

faq_plan.a: Write down the sections your clinicians read and which answers should reach a person before the visit. Describe both in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the form and the database behind it. Start with one section, check it on a phone, then add the rest.

faq_plan.q: Who completes the patient's medical history form?
faq_plan.ref: Who completes the patient's medical history form?

prov.original: Who completes the patient's medical history form?

faq_plan.a: The patient completes it. For a child, a parent or legal guardian fills it in, and an adult who needs help can have a family member or caregiver write the answers with them. A nurse or the doctor then reads it and asks about any answer that looks incomplete.

faq_plan.q: When should a medical history form template stand on its own?
faq_plan.a: Keep it separate when patients come back every year. A standalone history can be updated at each visit without redoing the rest of the packet. A first-visit intake form also asks who the person is, how to reach them, and why they came, and it can carry the history as one section.

faq_plan.q: How is a health screening form different from a medical history form?
faq_plan.a: A health screening form asks a short set of yes or no questions to make one decision, such as whether a camper or a new hire needs a follow-up before starting. A medical history form records a patient's full health background for a clinician. Keep a screening short, and send each yes to the person who makes the call.

faq_plan.q: What should a health screening form template ask?
faq_plan.a: A health screening form template should ask only what the decision needs: current conditions, medicines taken during the program, allergies with the reaction, and any limit on activity. Add an emergency contact and a signature from whoever fills it in. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps, even in the week every camper's form arrives.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find a free medical history form?
faq_plan.a: Start from a medical history form PDF that a hospital or clinic posts for its own patients, and adapt the questions to your practice. Match the length to the setting: a massage intake form needs only the health questions that change a session. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing a history form patients fill in online.

faq_plan.q: How to get a medical history form?
faq_plan.ref: How to get a medical history form?

prov.original: How to get a medical history form?

faq_plan.a: Ask the office you are visiting: it can send its form before the appointment or hand you one at the desk. To get a copy of your own history, ask your provider. Under the HIPAA Privacy Rule, you have a right to inspect and obtain a copy of the health information a covered provider keeps about you, with some exceptions. The office may require that request in writing.

Medical history forms are the pages a patient completes so a clinician knows their past health before treating them. The answers go into the patient's record. A doctor's office may ask for one at the first visit and for an update each year, and a surgery center may collect one before a procedure.

faq_plan.q: What is the format for a medical history form?
faq_plan.ref: What is the format for a medical history form?

prov.original: What is the format for a medical history form?

faq_plan.a: A medical history form is formatted as short sections, each on its own page or screen. Conditions get checkboxes, medications a table with name, dose, and schedule, and family history a row per relative. Patient details sit at the top, with the signature and date at the end. Send the link in the booking form confirmation so it is done before the visit.
